33.tq: Start with the secure Article 112–Budget pair and complete the consecutive financial-Article sequence.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: The Union Budget is prepared by the Budget Division of the
o: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
33.x: The Budget is prepared by the Budget Division in the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance.
33.tq: Apply the “which department does this job?” authority-identification method.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: The Annual Financial Statement of the Union is laid before Parliament by the
33.x: The Annual Financial Statement is laid before both Houses of Parliament by the President under the constitutional financial procedure.
33.tq: Distinguish the authority that formally lays the statement from the authority that prepares or presents it.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: The first Union Budget of independent India was presented by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty on
33.x: R. K. Shanmukham Chetty presented the first Union Budget of independent India on 26 November 1947.
33.tq: Use the date-person association rather than confusing the first Budget with later Budget-calendar changes.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: Since 2017, the Union Budget has generally been presented on
33.x: From 2017 onwards, the Union Budget has generally been presented on 1 February. The Budget for 2026–27 was presented on 1 February 2026.
33.tq: Test the change in the Budget presentation date against the earlier historical date.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s:
With reference to Demands for Grants, consider the following statements:
1. They are voted only by the Lok Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha may discuss them but cannot vote on them.
3. Charged expenditure is discussed but is not submitted to vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: All three statements are correct. Demands for Grants are voted by the Lok Sabha, while the Rajya Sabha can discuss them; charged expenditure is discussed but not voted upon.
33.tq: Separate voting power over demands from the power to discuss charged expenditure.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: In parliamentary financial procedure, the guillotine refers to
o: putting all outstanding demands to vote without discussion on the last day
the automatic rejection of all demands for grants
the President's power to withhold assent to a Money Bill
the referral of a financial Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
33.x: On the last day fixed for the discussion of demands, all outstanding demands are put to vote without further discussion. This procedure is called the guillotine.
33.tq: Recognise the procedural meaning of a specialised parliamentary term.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s:
Match the following types of cut motions with their purposes:

List-I (Cut motion)
A. Policy cut
B. Economy cut
C. Token cut

List-II (Purpose or amount)
1. Reduction by a specified amount to effect economy
2. Reduction of the demand to Re 1 to express disapproval of policy
3. Reduction by Rs 100 to ventilate a specific grievance

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
33.x: A policy cut reduces the demand to Re 1, an economy cut reduces it by a specified amount, and a token cut reduces it by Rs 100 to raise a specific grievance.
33.tq: Start from the distinctive numerical values—Re 1 and Rs 100—and then identify the remaining pair.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: A cut motion reducing a demand for grant to Re 1 signifies
o: a specific grievance against an individual minister
rejection of the entire Annual Financial Statement
disapproval of the policy underlying the demand
a demand for economy in expenditure
33.x: A policy cut motion proposes reducing the demand to Re 1 and expresses disapproval of the policy underlying the demand.
33.tq: Link the exact reduction amount with the purpose of the cut motion.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: Which of the following correctly describes a Vote on Account?
o: A vote by the Rajya Sabha on Demands for Grants
An advance grant for a part of the year until the Budget is passed
A permanent appropriation for the whole financial year
A grant available only for defence expenditure
33.x: A Vote on Account is an advance grant, usually for two months, to meet expenditure until the Budget is passed. It is provided under Article 116.
33.tq: Use the duration-and-purpose test to distinguish temporary authorisation from an annual appropriation.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s:
Consider the following statements about a Vote on Account:
1. It is provided under Article 116.
2. It is usually granted for two months.
3. It becomes unnecessary in election years because the Budget is presented on 1 February.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: A Vote on Account is covered by Article 116 and is usually granted for two months. It continues to be used in election years; the change to a 1 February Budget date has not made it ineffectual.
33.tq: Spot the false causal conclusion in statement 3 while retaining the article and duration facts.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s: The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025–26 included an Economic Stabilisation Fund of
33.x: The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025–26 included an Economic Stabilisation Fund of Rs 1 lakh crore.
33.tq: Retain the exact current-affairs figure and distinguish lakh crore from smaller crore amounts.
33.sec: Budget - Annual Financial Statement, Arts. 112-117, guillotine, cut motions, vote on account

33.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Formation of Andhra State
B. Introduction of the Andhra State Bill in Parliament
C. Assent to the Andhra State Bill
D. Presentation of the first Union Budget of independent India
33.x: The first Union Budget was presented on 26 November 1947, the Andhra State Bill was introduced on 10 August 1953, assent was given on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.
33.tq: Fix the earliest dated event first, then order the three Andhra State milestones.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: The Andhra State Bill was introduced in Parliament on
33.x: The Andhra State Bill was introduced in Parliament on 10 August 1953.
33.tq: Distinguish the introduction date from the assent date and the date of State formation.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the dates connected with the Andhra State Bill and the formation of Andhra State?
o: Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—14 September 1953; assent—10 August 1953; formation—1 October 1953
Introduction—10 August 1953; assent—1 October 1953; formation—14 September 1953
Introduction—1 October 1953; assent—14 September 1953; formation—10 August 1953
33.x: The Bill was introduced on 10 August 1953, received assent on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.
33.tq: Order the legislative process by introduction, assent and commencement rather than by memorising isolated dates.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, in relation to a Money Bill, can
o: refer it to a joint sitting within fourteen days
amend it finally within fourteen days
33.x: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council can only make recommendations on a Money Bill within fourteen days. It cannot reject or amend the Bill finally.
33.tq: Apply the special limitation on the Upper House of a State Legislature to a Money Bill.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: Under Article 200, the Governor may exercise which of the following options in relation to a Bill?
o: Refer every Bill directly to the Supreme Court
Return every Bill, including a Money Bill, for reconsideration
Dissolve the Legislative Assembly whenever a Bill is rejected
Assent, withhold assent, return a non-Money Bill, or reserve it for the President
33.x: The Governor's options under Article 200 include assent, withholding assent, returning a non-Money Bill for reconsideration, and reserving a Bill for the President. A Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration in the same manner.
33.tq: Use the authority-and-exception method, especially the distinction between Money Bills and non-Money Bills.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Articles 200 and 201?
o: Article 200 concerns the Governor's options on State Bills, while Article 201 concerns Bills reserved for the President
Article 200 concerns judicial review, while Article 201 concerns parliamentary privileges
Article 200 concerns Union Money Bills, while Article 201 concerns State Budgets
Both Articles exclusively regulate Constitutional Amendment Bills
33.x: Article 200 deals with the Governor's action on Bills passed by the State Legislature. Article 201 deals with Bills reserved for the consideration of the President.
33.tq: Compare the constitutional authority associated with each Article instead of confusing State and Union procedures.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: The five-judge Bench's advisory opinion on the Presidential Reference held that courts
o: can prescribe fixed timelines for Governors and declare deemed assent
must approve every Bill within fourteen days
cannot fix such timelines or declare deemed assent
can replace the Governor's decision with their own assent
33.x: The advisory opinion stated that courts cannot fix timelines for Governors in this context or declare deemed assent. It addressed the issues raised by the earlier debate on gubernatorial assent.
33.tq: Identify the precise legal conclusion and reject the reversed-power alternatives.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: The Supreme Court's five-judge Bench gave its opinion on the Presidential Reference concerning assent timelines in
33.x: The five-judge Bench's advisory opinion on the Presidential Reference was reported in November 2025. The Tamil Nadu Governor judgment itself was delivered in April 2025.
33.tq: Separate the date of the earlier Governor judgment from the later Presidential Reference opinion.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 sought to change the name of Kerala to
33.x: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 sought to change the name of the State to “Keralam”.
33.tq: Test the exact proposed name rather than the historical names of the region.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 is associated constitutionally with
33.x: The alteration of the name of a State is dealt with under Article 3. The Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon Session of 2026.
33.tq: Match the territorial-change subject with the relevant constitutional Article.
33.sec: Universal angles

33.s: During the Monsoon Session of 2026, the Rajya Sabha also passed the
33.x: The Rajya Sabha passed the NCDC (Amendment) Bill, 2026 during the Monsoon Session of 2026. The FCRA Bill was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee rather than receiving final assent in that session.
33.tq: Distinguish a Bill passed by the House from one merely referred to a committee.
33.sec: Universal angles

34.s: Under which Article of the Constitution is the Consolidated Fund of India provided for?
34.x: Article 266(1) provides for the Consolidated Fund of India. It includes revenues received by the Union, loans raised by it and loan repayments received by it.
34.tq: Use the Article-number distinction between the two parts of Article 266 and Article 267.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: Which one of the following expenditures from the Consolidated Fund of India requires an appropriation law?
o: Withdrawal for an unforeseen expenditure pending parliamentary approval
Withdrawal of amounts credited to the Consolidated Fund for government expenditure
Remittance of money held temporarily in the Public Account
Withdrawal of public deposits held by the government as trustee
34.x: Money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India only under an appropriation made by law. The Contingency Fund and Public Account follow different rules.
34.tq: Identify the fund first, then apply its withdrawal rule.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Consolidated Fund of India:
1. It includes all revenues received by the Union Government.
2. It includes loans raised by the Union Government, including Treasury Bills and internal or external loans.
3. It includes repayments of loans received by the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. The Consolidated Fund comprises Union revenues, loans raised through specified sources and loan repayments received by the Union.
34.tq: Check whether each statement covers a separate component of the same constitutional fund.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the Public Account of India?
1. Provident funds — amounts held by the government in a fiduciary capacity
2. Small savings — amounts credited to the Public Account
3. Deposits and remittances — transactions included in the Public Account
4. Withdrawal — requires an appropriation law in every case
34.x: Provident funds, small savings, deposits and remittances are credited to the Public Account. Withdrawal from it does not require appropriation in the same manner as withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund, making statement 4 incorrect.
34.tq: Find the statement that reverses the constitutional rule applicable to the Public Account.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: In relation to the Public Account of India, the Government primarily acts as a
34.x: The Government acts as a banker or trustee in respect of money credited to the Public Account, such as provident funds, deposits and small savings.
34.tq: Test the functional role associated with the fund rather than merely its contents.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: The Contingency Fund of India is intended primarily for meeting
o: routine departmental expenditure included in the annual budget
expenditure from public deposits without legislative scrutiny
unforeseen expenditure pending approval by Parliament
repayment of all external loans raised by the Union
34.x: The Contingency Fund is used for unforeseen expenditure when immediate action is necessary, pending authorisation by Parliament.
34.tq: Distinguish emergency advances from routine budgetary expenditure and loan transactions.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s:
Consider the following statements about the Contingency Fund of India:
1. It is provided for under Article 267 of the Constitution.
2. It was established under the Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950.
3. It is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Expenditure.
4. It is at the disposal of the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All four statements are correct. Article 267 provides for the Fund, which was established by the 1950 Act, is held by the Finance Secretary in the Department of Economic Affairs, and is placed at the President’s disposal.
34.tq: Separate the constitutional provision, establishing law, custody and operational authority.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: What is the corpus of the Contingency Fund of India stated for the financial year 2021-22 onwards?
34.x: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was raised to ₹30,000 crore from the financial year 2021-22.
34.tq: Distinguish the present corpus from the earlier corpus and from larger budgetary figures.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: Which one of the following statements regarding audit of government funds is correct?
o: The CAG audits all three funds of the Union and the States.
The CAG audits the Consolidated and Public Accounts but not Contingency Funds.
The Finance Secretary audits all three funds and reports to the CAG.
The CAG audits only the Consolidated Fund of India.
34.x: The Comptroller and Auditor General audits the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account of both the Union and the States.
34.tq: Watch for the exclusion of one fund and identify the constitutional audit authority.
34.sec: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account

34.s: The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in
34.x: The separate Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in 2017. It had been separated in 1924 on the recommendation of the Acworth Committee.
34.tq: Use the paired historical dates to distinguish separation from merger.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The separation of the Railway Budget from the General Budget in 1924 was based on the recommendation of the
34.x: The Railway Budget was separated from the General Budget in 1924 on the recommendation of the Acworth Committee.
34.tq: Apply the wrong-committee trap to a well-known budget reform.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: Which one of the following changes was associated with the Union Budget from 2017-18?
o: Introduction of the first Outcome Budget
Introduction of the Railway Budget as a separate document
Dropping of the Plan and Non-Plan distinction
Restoration of the Plan and Non-Plan distinction
34.x: The Plan and Non-Plan distinction was dropped from 2017-18. This was distinct from the earlier introduction of the Outcome Budget in 2005.
34.tq: Discriminate between reforms introduced in different years.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The Outcome Budget, also known as the Output-Outcome Framework, was introduced in
34.x: The Outcome Budget was introduced in 2005 and is treated as a budget document under the Output-Outcome Framework.
34.tq: Separate the year of introduction from the later Railway Budget and Plan distinction reforms.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: Which of the following best describes gender budgeting?
o: Allocation of the entire budget exclusively to women-specific departments
Allocation of resources with reference to gender where disparities are chronic
Allocation of funds only for female employment schemes
Preparation of a separate budget for women outside the Union Budget
34.x: Gender budgeting involves making allocations with reference to gender in areas where gender disparities are chronic. It is not restricted to an entirely separate or women-only budget.
34.tq: Reject the extreme ‘entirely’ and ‘only’ interpretations of a policy concept.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The Gender Budget Statement has been presented since
34.x: The Gender Budget Statement has been presented since 2005-06 as part of the gender-budgeting process.
34.tq: Distinguish the financial year of the statement from the year of Railway Budget merger.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Performance budgeting — First Hoover Commission and Administrative Reforms Commission
2. Zero-Based Budgeting — Peter Pyhrr
3. First use of Zero-Based Budgeting in government — Jimmy Carter
4. Outcome Budget — Acworth Committee
34.x: Performance budgeting is associated with the First Hoover Commission in the USA and the Administrative Reforms Commission in India. Zero-Based Budgeting is associated with Peter Pyhrr and was first used by Jimmy Carter; the Acworth Committee was related to the Railway Budget separation, not Outcome Budget.
34.tq: Use the person-committee-purpose trap by matching each reform with its proper association.
34.sec: Railway budget merger, outcome budget, gender budget

34.s: The Union Budget for 2026-27 was presented on
34.x: The Union Budget 2026-27 was presented on 1 February 2026. The date 14 February 2026 relates to the presentation of the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27.
34.tq: Separate closely placed Union and State budget dates.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: Which group of Articles is identified as containing budget-related provisions?
34.x: The budget-related provisions identified here are Articles 109 to 117 and Articles 265 to 267, covering financial legislation, public revenues and the principal government funds.
34.tq: Check the complete range rather than selecting an option containing only familiar financial Articles.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26 approved by the Lok Sabha is associated with
34.x: Supplementary, additional or excess grants are provided for under Article 115. The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2025-26 was approved by the Lok Sabha.
34.tq: Use the Article-function association and distinguish supplementary grants from the Annual Financial Statement.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: The proposed Economic Stabilisation Fund of ₹1 lakh crore was intended to address
o: only agricultural subsidies in the States
capital expenditure on railway tracks alone
repayment of all public-sector bank loans
34.x: The proposed Economic Stabilisation Fund of ₹1 lakh crore was intended to respond to global shocks and disruptions in supply chains.
34.tq: Match the proposed fund with its stated purpose and reject narrow or absolute alternatives.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s: Who presented the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27?
34.x: The Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 was presented on 14 February 2026 by Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav.
34.tq: Apply the office-holder trap by distinguishing the Finance Minister, the Agriculture Minister and the Governor.
34.sec: Universal angles

34.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27:
1. A separate Agriculture Budget was presented by K. Atchannaidu.
2. The session opened with the address of Governor S. Abdul Nazeer to both Houses.
3. The Budget was presented on 14 February 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: All three statements are correct. K. Atchannaidu presented the separate Agriculture Budget, Governor S. Abdul Nazeer addressed both Houses at the opening, and the State Budget was presented on 14 February 2026.
34.tq: Verify the date, presenter and opening constitutional act as separate facts before choosing the combination.
